summary: The reported api-gateway symptom is a downstream effect. Onset was ~09:45-09:53Z. Config change cfg-2207 (infra-automation, cost-optimisation profile 'small') reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52Z. Normal steady load (~560 req/s, ~12 needed concurrent connections) immediately exceeded the 5-connection ceiling; the HikariPool saturated (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting up to 57), request acquisition timed out at 3000ms, first error 09:53:19Z. portfolio-service p99 rose to ~4.2s and 5xx to ~22%, and api-gateway then returned 504 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' with p99 >4s. The human-suspected gateway HTTP/2 deploy (dep-5220, 08:00Z) is contradicted: onset was ~1h45m later after flat latency, and order-service received the same h2 change with no impact. Root cause is a config_change originating in portfolio-service.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Cost-optimisation config shrank portfolio-service DB pool to 5, causing pool exhaustion
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-2207 (infra-automation cost-optimisation profile 'small') reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52Z. Normal steady load of ~560 req/s needs ~12 concurrent connections; with only 5 the HikariPool saturates (active=5, idle=0, waiting 25-57), requests block up to the 3000ms acquisition timeout, portfolio-service p99 rises to ~4.2s and 500s climb to ~22%, and api-gateway times out upstream returning 504s on /v1/portfolio/*.

causal_chain.claim: pool ceiling now 5 while peak requirement was ~12 in-use
connections exhaust: total=5 active=5 idle=0, waiters queue and hit 3000ms timeout
gateway upstream timeouts -> 504 on portfolio routes, gateway p99 up

assumptions: No other concurrent change to portfolio-service or ledger-db
The 'small' profile's max_size=5 matches the observed total=5 pool ceiling
Baseline ~12 in-use is representative of normal demand

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220) to upstreams caused the outage
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 08:00Z api-gateway envoy upgrade enabling HTTP/2 to upstreams introduced a fault that stalls portfolio-service calls, driving gateway p99 >4s and 504s.
assumptions: HTTP/2 could selectively affect only portfolio paths
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Onset was ~1h45m after the deploy with completely flat latency in between (F9 vs F1); order-service received the same h2 change but shows zero impact (F10); the errors are explicit DB connection-pool exhaustion in portfolio-service (F3) tied to a config change 1 minute before onset (F5/F13). And in a separate check I searched order-service and it showed no latency impact. The gateway is a downstream victim, not the origin.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db / infrastructure degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A ledger-db (shared datastore) slowdown or failover caused portfolio-service query slowness and timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Error messages are client-side pool acquisition failures (total=5), not DB-side errors/timeouts; the pool in-use value is clamped at exactly 5 matching the config, and portfolio had no restarts. A DB-side problem would not produce a pool ceiling of exactly 5.

facts.statement: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size was changed from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z by cfg-2207 (cost-optimisation profile).
The first JDBC acquisition failure in portfolio-service was at 09:53:19Z, ~1 minute after the config change.
portfolio-service HikariPool is exhausted at total=5, active=5, idle=0 with many waiters.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use is pinned at exactly 5.0 from 10:00 onward vs ~12 before.
portfolio-service p99 jumped to ~4.2s at 09:45 and error_rate to ~22%.
api-gateway p99 jumped to ~4.3s and emits 504 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' on /v1/portfolio/holdings.
order-service, which also got the HTTP/2 change, shows no latency impact.
portfolio-service request rate (~560 req/s) and CPU (~36%) were steady, and restarts were zero.

assumptions: No other concurrent change to portfolio-service or ledger-db occurred around 09:52Z.
Baseline db_pool_in_use ~12 is representative of normal portfolio-service demand.
The observed HikariPool total=5 is the direct result of cfg-2207's max_size=5.
(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The gateway HTTP/2 deploy was at 08:00Z, ~1h45m before onset, and also covered order-service.

timeline.event: api-gateway deploy dep-5220 (envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service).
portfolio-service and api-gateway latency begin rising (p99 into seconds).
cfg-2207 applies cost-optimisation profile: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5.
First portfolio-service error: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms'.
HikariPool exhaustion errors: total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43.
db_pool_in_use pinned at 5.0; error_rate ~22% steady; incident ongoing to current time.

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 5 back to 50 (or appropriate value).
recommended_actions.rationale: Pool ceiling of 5 directly matches the observed exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0); restoring capacity should relieve the incident.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT prioritize rolling back gateway dep-5220; it is not the cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: Onset lag, unaffected order-service, and the DB pool errors show the gateway deploy is unrelated.

recommended_actions.action: Add guardrails/validation to infra-automation cost-optimisation profiles so pool sizes cannot be reduced below measured peak demand.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevent recurrence of the same class of config regression (cf. HIST-115).

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on HikariPool active/total saturation and db pool wait time so exhaustion is detected before user-visible 504s.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool saturated at 09:53 but the user-facing incident was noticed later; earlier detection shortens MTTR.

data_gaps: No ledger-db telemetry was queried directly; a DB-side contribution cannot be fully excluded, though client-side pool errors and the exact 5-connection ceiling strongly argue against it.
Only portfolio-service and order-service config/deploys were inspected in detail; a change on another shared component (ledger-db, redis-cache) was not exhaustively ruled out.
The exact mapping of the 'small' cost-optimisation profile values was not independently confirmed against cfg-2207 beyond max_size=5.

api-gateway p99 latency jumped from ~210ms to ~4300ms over the same 09:45 window, with p99 peaks ~4700ms.
portfolio-service Hikari connection pool is exhausted at exactly 5 connections: 'total=5, active=5, idle=0' with dozens of waiters.

findings.statement: Config change cfg-2207 on portfolio-service set db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z, described as applying a cost-optimisation profile.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was ~12 before the change and pinned exactly at 5.0 from 10:00 onward (the new pool ceiling).
portfolio-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~22% (5xx) starting in the 09:45 bucket.
api-gateway 504s are specifically 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings', i.e. the gateway fails while waiting on portfolio-service.
The gateway HTTP/2 deploy (dep-5220) landed at 08:00:00Z, ~1h45m before onset, and applied to both portfolio-service and order-service.

findings.statement: order-service, which also received the gateway HTTP/2 upstream change, shows flat p99 (~150ms) throughout the incident window.
portfolio-service request rate stayed steady at ~560 req/s before and during the incident, and CPU stayed ~36% — no traffic surge or CPU pressure.
portfolio-service had zero restarts throughout the window, ruling out a crash/restart loop.
The onset of pool exhaustion (first JDBC error 09:53:19Z) follows the pool-shrink config change (09:52:00Z) by ~1 minute, far tighter than the 08:00 deploy.
